body:
Priya (Support): ACME flagged a sharp increase in tail latency on hosted inference in eu-central yesterday evening. p95 went from ~140ms to 1.5s, p99 into 2.5s+ and some 503s. ticket attached.
ACME (Customer): started around 2024-11-03 19:40 CET after our nightly batch. high variance, retries spike. sending sample request ids.
Priya (Support): sample ids: req_ab12cd34, req_ab12cd35. their usage pattern: steady inference + periodic heavy embedding job at 19:35.
Noah (SRE): pulling infra metrics now. shows a cluster-wide p95 jump at 19:36 correlated with host-level iowait and NVMe write latency for a subset of nodes. AlertBot also triggered disk_high_lat at 19:38.
Ravi (Oncall): I'll start collecting node diagnostics (iostat, nvme fw-log, dmesg). can someone check recent infra changes?
Ethan (Infra): we applied a rolling OS update last night: kernel 6.5.8 and a CUDA driver update 12.3.2 to our inference pool at ~18:45 UTC. Also pushed NVMe firmware 2.4.1 to some hosts as part of a storage vendor advisory at ~19:00 UTC.
Sofia (Eng-runtime): runtime pattern: KV cache writes and small checkpoint flushes produce many small sync writes under pressure. if the block layer starts deferring/queueing differently, we'd see spikes. saw similar on staging when kernel scheduler changed.
Noah (SRE): attaching dmesg snippet from host-12:

```
Nov  3 19:39:12 host-12 kernel: nvme0: I/O 234567 queued beyond capacity
Nov  3 19:39:12 host-12 kernel: nvme0n1: aborting command
Nov  3 19:39:13 host-12 kernel: nvme0: controller reset due to I/O error
Nov  3 19:39:34 host-12 kernel: INFO: task kworker/3:5 blocked for more than 120 seconds
```

Ravi (Oncall): ok root cause hypothesis: interaction between new kernel scheduling defaults + NVMe fw behavior causing controller resets under mixed read/write load, leading to spikes and occasional 503s when runtime stalls.
Ethan (Infra): confirmed: some nodes show changed elevator to "none" (blk-mq default) while others kept mq-deadline. vendor release notes for fw 2.4.1 mention changes to submission queue limits.
Sofia (Eng-runtime): can we reproduce on a canary? I'll prepare a repeatable script that simulates small sync writes + inference.
Noah (SRE): yes please. repro steps we used:
1) background small-writer: 8 threads writing 2kB files in tight loop to /var/lib/redwood/kv
2) run inference load with concurrency=800, batch=2 for 10m
3) monitor nvme latencies, dmesg, top
commands:
```
# small writer (background)
for i in {1..8}; do while true; do dd if=/dev/zero of=/var/lib/redwood/kv/f$i bs=2k count=1 oflag=dsync; done & done
# loadgen (container)
redwood-loadgen --model /models/llama-13b --concurrency 800 --batch 2 --seq 256 --duration 600
# monitor
iostat -x 1 > /tmp/iostat.log &
nvme fw-log /dev/nvme0 > /tmp/fwlog && dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg_tail
```

Ethan (Infra): ran repro on canary host-22: reproduced high write latency and occasional controller reset after ~4m. changing /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler to mq-deadline reduced tail from ~2s -> ~220ms.
Noah (SRE): mitigation plan (short term):
- immediately taint affected hosts to prevent new pods: `kubectl taint nodes host-22 infra/unstable=true:NoSchedule`
- set scheduler to mq-deadline on affected hosts (tested on canary): `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler`
- reduce NVMe queue depth if controller is overcommitting: `echo 32 > /sys/block/nvme0/device/queue_depth`
- push runtime config to ACME's dedicated pool to coalesce KV writes (hot flag)
- if needed, rollback NVMe firmware to 2.2.x (requires reboot/maintenance window)

Sofia (Eng-runtime): I can push a hotfix flag to increase write coalescing and disable immediate fsyncs for non-critical paths. deploying now to dedicated nodes; should reduce small sync writes in ~45s.
AlertBot: Config change deployed to pool-dedicated-eu-central by Sofia.
Ravi (Oncall): I'll coordinate node isolation and make sure we only change live sysfs on canaries first. Noah, please prepare an ops runbook with exact commands and sanity checks.
Noah (SRE): runbook snippet:
```
# isolate node
kubectl taint nodes host-22 infra/unstable=true:NoSchedule
kubectl cordon host-22
# change scheduler (live, canary first)
echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler
# reduce queue depth
echo 32 > /sys/block/nvme0/device/queue_depth
# verify
cat /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler
cat /sys/block/nvme0/device/queue_depth
# rollback driver (if required)
dpkg -i /var/cache/packages/cuda-driver_12.3.1.deb && systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
```

Ethan (Infra): note: changing scheduler on-live can cause transient IO changes; do on canary first. queue_depth tune reduced throughput on canary but improved p99 significantly.
ACME (Customer): saw improvement after the hotfix and node isolation — p95 back to ~160ms and p99 down to ~420ms for now, thanks. we'll keep monitoring.
Priya (Support): passing update to CS. ACME asked about root cause and vendor timeline.
Noah (SRE): next steps:
- open INF ticket INF-3832 with collected dmesg, iostat, nvme fw logs, and repro script; escalate to NVMe vendor + distro kernel team
- plan firmware rollback for affected nodes in nightly maintenance if vendor recommends rollback (requires reboots)
- add nvme fw/version + /sys/block/*/queue/scheduler checks to node exporter, alert if mismatch or lat > 300ms for > 30s
- add an infra CI perf test that runs mixed small-writes + inference during image validation to catch this regression earlier
Sofia (Eng-runtime): I'll make the runtime flag permanent for dedicated pools and add metrics for small write bursts so we can alarm earlier.
Ethan (Infra): scheduling firmware rollback window for 6 hosts tomorrow 02:00 UTC; will coordinate with support and oncall.
Ravi (Oncall): keeping channel open until rollout complete and ACME confirms stable.
Noah (SRE): TL;DR root cause = interaction between kernel blk-mq defaults in 6.5.x, NVMe fw 2.4.x queue behavior, and runtime small synchronous writes causing controller resets and host stalls. mitigations applied: node isolation, scheduler change, runtime coalesce, and planned firmware rollback.
Priya (Support): thanks team. ACME is monitoring and we'll reopen if any regression. :heart:
